text:
Evelyn: Heads-up — we got a customer report that Org `acme-inc` saw repeated 429s this morning. They say it happens when another tenant in the same shard blasts a burst.
Jasper: I saw the same in telemetry — overall shard utilization fine but per-org tail spiking. looks like our smoothing is too global.
Mira: Can you paste the trace? rough timeline + affected model + keys?
Evelyn: Pasted snippets: shard-42, model:gpt-open-7b, 08:12-08:18 window. A single apiKey had 8x normal QPS for ~90s, then other orgs dropped to stay within shard cap.
Sanjay: This is the classic noisy-neighbor problem. Current enforcement: per-shard hard cap -> fair-share by weighted smoothing. That gives strong guarantees for steady state but penalizes short bursts from well-behaved orgs.
Isla: We need to balance two things: protecting latency SLO for steady workloads, and allowing legitimate short bursts (e.g., product demos). Proposal: add a per-key burst allowance + adaptive smoothing that decays on a per-org basis.
Ravi: +1. Also need observability: console should show a "throttle rationale" bubble with: reason (global cap | per-org smoothing | burst-exceeded), metrics used, and when limits will relax.
infra-bot: Incident detected: "per-org-throttle" shard-42 (1760251234). Auto-ticket created: #ops-2431.
Jasper: For detection, I suggest a "burst_score" computed as: burst_score = max(0, (p99_qps_last_60s / median_qps_last_1h) - 1). If burst_score > 4 for >30s -> mark as bursting.
Mira: That metric is simple and explainable. But it can misfire for small orgs with noisy medians. Maybe use an EMA baseline with min_samples threshold.
Evelyn: Agreed. Also want a smoothing policy config sample to discuss. Example config: ```json
{
  "per_org": {
    "smoothing_window_sec": 60,
    "alpha": 0.4,
    "max_burst_tokens": 2000,
    "burst_detection_threshold": 4
  },
  "shard": {
    "hard_cap_qps": 10000,
    "fair_share_policy": "weighted"
  }
}
```
Sanjay: Two enforcement modes: optimistic allow-then-throttle (accept extra tokens, bill, then retro-throttle via smoothing) vs conservative deny-on-burst. I prefer optimistic for UX but we need guardrails to avoid ripple.
Isla: UX note: console should display a per-org "burst budget" countdown and an option to request temporary burst increase (manual approve or auto-grant based on past behavior).
Ravi: For auto-grants: criterion could be 1) org has <2 throttles in last 30d, 2) average error-rate <1%, 3) not already at reserve usage. If auto-grant, set a soft limit for 2 minutes.
Mira: Telemetry changes: add an event type `burst_event` with fields: org, apiKey, shard, p50, p95, p99, baseline_ema, burst_score, burst_start_ts. We can then power dashboards and alerts.
Evelyn: On fairness: smoothing should operate per-org, not per-shard, so a single noisy key only reduces its own smoothed allowance instead of lowering the global smoothing factor. That way neighbors are protected.
Jasper: Implementation note: our current token-bucket allocator runs at shard level. To do per-org smoothing we can maintain per-org virtual tokens within the shard token-bucket and periodically reconcile. This keeps allocator hot path cheap.
Isla: Also add a "fairness score" in the console showing historical impact of other tenants on an org (e.g., % of time under target latency attributable to neighbor-induced throttles). Helpful for sales + support.
Ravi: Any objections to merging a PoC that: 1) implements burst_score detection, 2) per-org smoothing window, 3) dashboard panels + throttle rationale text?
Mira: No objections. I'd like unit tests for edge cases: tiny orgs, very spiky demo traffic, quota transitions during rollouts.
Sanjay: plan: small PoC on non-prod shard, run synthetic noise + happy path, review perf impact. If good, roll canary to one region.
Evelyn: Sounds good. I'll open a tracking RFC and include the config + telemetry schema.
Jasper: Thanks — if anyone wants to pair on the allocator change ping me.
Isla: I'll mock up the console UX and the burst budget widget this afternoon. :sparkles:
Ravi: I'll draft the auto-grant rules and ops playbook.
Evelyn: Closing loop: owners = Jasper (allocator), Isla (console), Ravi (policy), Mira (telemetry). We'll reconvene after PoC run.
infra-bot: Ticket created: RFC-7592 "per-org burst fairness & dashboard" assigned to Jasper. Deadline: 2 weeks.
